newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says OPEC should curtail over-production.
newsitem.headline: Iran says OPEC should curtail over-production.

text.p: OPEC should take measures to curtail over-production to help shore up oil prices in the remaining months of this year, Iran's Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh was quoted as saying on Sunday.
"The oil market normally faces a slump in spring, but the improvement of the situation depends on OPEC itself," he said.

"It should take proper measures to prevent any new increase in production, and through this we hope prices will be improved during the remaining months of the year," he told the English-language Kayhan International daily.
He said the partial return of Iraq to the oil market had "very limited" impact on prices. "Our greatest problem in OPEC is not Iraq, but the internal discipline and the observation of quotas."
He was speaking ahead of OPEC's ministerial meeting in Vienna next week, where member states are due to debate the sharp slide in oil prices this year.

Widespread quota-busting has lifted OPEC output two million bpd above its self-imposed ceiling of 25.03 million bpd but traders are betting on an extension of current allocations for another six months and see little progress on discipline at the meeting.
Traders said price hawks led by OPEC's second biggest exporter Iran may want to make an issue out of quota compliance but they warned that a public showdown could scare markets into further losses.
